#1937. Bradford City boss Michael Duff on working relationship with Alex Morris - and praise for stalwart duo

Alexander's partnership with assistant Chris Lucketti was a winning one, with coaches Mark Trueman and Colin Doyle also being key components to the Bantams' upturn.

Early days it may be for Duff, but the Bantams chief is quick to value the input of his own number two in Alex Morris and the aforesaid coaching duo who have been stalwarts at the club in recent years.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Duff, whose side are preparing for back-to-back home league derbies with Doncaster Rovers and Barnsley, said: "Truey's been in the club for a long time and worked under a few managers.

"Quite often it can be: 'Oh, here we go, here's another one, what's he going to do, what's he going to say?'

"But I've had some good conversations with Truey and him and Doyler have been really, really good. But they couldn't beat me and Alex at padel, I'll throw that one in!

"Sometimes, it's little things in training. We review every training session and sometimes it's a case of 'Well, they wouldn't have been used to that because of this' or 'They might not like that because of this'.

"It's like: 'Okay, well that's good to know.' That's where we (Duff and Morris) may need to check ourselves and go: 'Okay, what's the best thing for the team ultimately'."

Duff and Morris enjoyed a strong working relationship during their time together at previous club Wycombe Wanderers, with Duff moving quickly to sound out Morris about heading north and renewing their union when the opportunity presented itself at Valley Parade.

He acknowledges that his deputy is particularly important for daily dialogue with players, as his assistant position allows him to develop a more up-close-and-personal relationship.

The City boss continued: "Alex spends a lot more time with the players than I do because he's around them a lot more often and they'll probably have more personal conversations with Alex. It's something he's very good at.

"I try to, but obviously sometimes when you speak to a player, it's like: 'Well, he's the headmaster, so tell him what he wants and get out,' which I don't want it to be like that. But that's just the natural evolution of my job.

"Alex is good for many different reasons. Tactically, he's very, very good and has been coaching for a long, long time.

"He's coached at a high level. He's worked with League Two players and worked at Championship level, so he can put on different sessions and knows what the group needs and knows me as well.

"Sometimes that's where assistants are really good, because it's like: 'I know you want to do this, but this might not be right at the moment'. And that's where sometimes I have to check my own ego, because it's not about me.

"He's a really good sort of sounding board because he knows me really well."

#1936. Norway manager explains reason for ‘terribly tame’ Martin Odegaard performance

Arsenal skipper Martin Odegaard was accused of delivering a ‘terribly tame’ performance for Norway in their Nations League win over Wales.

The Gunners’ captian completed 90 minutes as Stale Solbakken’s side ran out comfortable 3-1 winners courtesy of goals from Antonio Nusa, Andreas Schjelderup and Erling Haaland.

Odegaard, however, appeared far from his usual energetic self and his lack of spark was noted by former Norway international Kjetil Rekdal.

‘I think he was terribly tame today,’ Rekdal told TV 2. ‘He looked tired and didn’t have the movement he usually has.

‘I think he was much less visible than he usually is.’

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Solbakken, however, explained that his inspirational playmaker overcame an illness that caused Odegaard to endure a sleepless night prior to the match.

‘We have had a captain who has been lying around all night and spitting, and who was allowed to take some other liberties than he was supposed to,’ he said.

‘If you lie down all night and throw up, that’s it. All credit to him for going the distance. We had a conversation during the break that he should just drive from the start and let us know when the tank was empty.’

Odegaard’s commitment to the cause was praised by several of his teammates, including David Moller Wolfe.

Patrick Berg star, who started on the bench, but came on in the second half, added: ‘I understood that Martin had a bad night.

#1935. Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR

Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7

Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

The final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

Victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i

The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

When Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

Gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

For 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

Bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

Bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

Should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

Just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

Tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

Bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

Possession: Aston Villa 45%-55% Bayern MunichShots: 4-7Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 1-2

The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

Aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

The German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

That is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

Bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

That was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder shows good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

Bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

Bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

Aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is currently out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

The ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

The first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

Chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

Currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

Aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

Bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

#1934. Barnsley's Patrick Kelly hoping Northern Ireland can soon be among Nations League big fish

Two years after winning their League C group to return to the second tier, Northern Ireland go into Tuesday’s match away to Hungary knowing they will be elevated to League A if they avoid defeat in Budapest.

The turnaround in Northern Ireland’s fortunes in this competition have been stark – prior to coming back up from League C they had just one win in 16 Nations League matches – but this young squad have taken huge steps forward since then.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Asked if he could have predicted Northern Ireland would be in this position with one game left, Barnsley midfielder Kelly told the Press Association: “I wouldn’t say I expected it but I wouldn’t have been shocked.

“I know we have a really good group and we fancy ourselves up against anyone and thankfully results have kind of gone our way and we’ve put ourselves in a really good position.”

The prospect of moving to the top tier of European football is a huge prize to put in front of this young side.

The 22-year-old Kelly’s most memorable moment in international football to date came with his fine goal in a 3-1 friendly defeat by France in June. Competitive fixtures against nations of that calibre would be the norm in League A.

“I think that’s a big incentive,” Kelly said. “It’ll just put us in a really good place if we can top the group, that’ll be a really strong finish to the campaign.

“Playing against teams like France, England, Spain, that would be good to test yourself at that level, to play against them more often and kind of see where we are.”

Northern Ireland will have to deal with two key suspensions in Budapest, with manager Michael O’Neill needing to watch from the sidelines after picking up a touchline ban, while striker Jamie Donley – who has travelled to Hungary – is also out after getting his second booking.

Kelly said he was not worried about O’Neill’s ban.

“Not much changes,” he said. “We’ll just have our game plan ready and go in and try to produce that,” he said. “We’ll just be ready to play the game.”

Donley’s suspension could offer a bigger role to Kelly with O’Neill weighing how to rejig his attacking options without the man who has led the line throughout this campaign.

“We’ve been working on it now,” Kelly said. “We’re not 100 per cent sure who is going to do that yet. Jamie will be a big miss for us but we’ve got a good squad and whoever’s called upon will be able to go in there and try to replicate what he’s been doing really well for us.”

#1933. Worthing Women: Make Mackay-ne a double!

Nicole Mackay’s brace made it three goals in two games for her and a second successive win for Worthing Women, as they saw off Aylesford at the Sussex Transport Community Stadium.

After last week’s epic cup comeback at Camden, teenage starlet Hattie Rainey made her full debut while Ruby Murdock also came into the starting eleven; meaning that Skye Birkinshaw and Cristie Pritchard began on the bench.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Barely had supporters sat in their seats than the aforementioned Mackay got the home team off and running, just three minutes in.

Seizing on  a loose ball on the edge of the eighteen yard area, the in-form striker drilled low and hard into Aylesford ‘keeper Sade Rider’s bottom right-hand corner, to open the scoring in emphatic fashion.

Although a very different picture might have been painted had the Rebels's netminder Sian Woods not denied a clean through Leigha Bradding-Butler not once but twice, to deny the visitor’s top scorer a seventh strike of a prolific campaign.

Still inside the opening ten minutes, Mackay came the width of the crossbar away from extending the host’s advantage. Dusting herself down and stepping up to take a free-kick she herself had won, the ball cannoned back off the frame of the goal, with Jess Richardson landing the rebound on top of the net.

The game settled into a more even contest for some time after that, as Worthing pressed forward in search of a second before the break, with Aylesford looking dangerous on the counter-attack.

Approaching the half-time interval, an audible sigh of relief reverberated around Woodside Road via Immy Armstrong - a threat from her set-pieces - firing narrowly over the target from inside the penalty area.

The sun then broke through the clouds on a pleasant November afternoon; similar to the way in which Aliyah Sheridan did when gifted possession by the homester’s otherwise solid last line of defence. Woods redeemed herself via a strong parry to her left of Sheridan’s subsequent shot.

One final opportunity before the change of ends fell to visiting Skipper Ami Burnham, only for Woods to keep her out by way of another excellent stop.

It’s tight at the bottom of the London & South East Prem but it was the Reds who headed into the interval with a precious one-goal lead.

Worthing continued to probe and were rewarded just shy of the hour mark, thanks to the persistence of Mackay. Although it was centre-half Ella Terry who got the ball rolling, courtesy of a wonderful switch of play from the middle of the park out to the roving Richardson on the right flank. The winger then found a well-placed Mackay to test Rider in the travellers’ net, with the Kent club’s custodian unable to prevent the Rebel’s number nineteen from overtaking Amber Hazlewood as leading markswoman in a red (occasionally lilac) shirt.

Some fine build-up laid the foundations for a possible third not long afterwards, when a Hattie Rainey pass went from a central position to wide on the right again, releasing the rapid Richardson to, ultimately, find Mackay once more, with the forward teeing up Neve McEvaddy for a long-range piledriver which saw Rider pull off a terrific save.

Goalscorer nearly turned provider three-quarters of the way into the contest but neither Richardson nor Annie Gracey could apply the finishing  touch to a dangerous-looking delivery.

Almost instantly, the visiting Blues hit back via a neat move of their own, culminating in half-time substitute Kara Richardson forcing Woods to hold on.

Ten to go and another excellent long ball from Terry resulted in some equally impressive hold-up play by the recently-introduced Paige Baker-Carroll, providing Richardson with an opening that she couldn’t quite keep down.

Not over the line yet though, the home side were reminded of the threat carried by Aylesford when Bradding-Bulter’s corner eventually led to Kara Richardson drawing a one-handed stop out of Woods, at the (in)expense of another flag-kick.

Time was running out for the girls from the Garden of England and Armstrong was quick to pounce on Pritchard's pass to fellow replacement Megan Gates; although the final flourish from twenty yards failed to test Woods between the home posts.

Fittingly, Worthing’s brightly-clad netminder had the last word on proceedings, as she added to her collection of wonder saves by frustrating Sheridan with only a few short minutes of normal time to play.

That would, indeed, be that and three vital points stayed at the Sussex Transport Community Stadium to move the Rebels up to ninth in the table, ahead of another tough test at bottom-of-the-table and fellow Sussex side Eastbourne Borough next Sunday.

#1932. Cardinale clarifies his ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ statement: “Lead the club into a new era”

Gerry Cardinale has clarified his ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ statement from about three years ago, stating that investments and resources are needed to get AC Milan back to the top.

Back in September 2023, a little over a year after he completed the purchase of Milan, Cardinale sat down with Corriere della Sera to explain his project for the club. “In football I want to be a Berlusconi 2.0, to have the same impact as him in a completely changed context,” he said, among other things.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s a quote that didn’t land brilliantly with some of the Milan fans, who felt that Cardinale grossly underestimated how much work Berlusconi put in with the throwaway comment. It was more than just a throwaway comment, though.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, following the launch of Milan’s new holding company MSE, Cardinale clarified what he meant by the quote. It was not meant as an arrogant comparison, but rather as praise for Berlusconi and what he can learn from the legendary Milan owner.

The connection with Milan deserves a separate mention: RedBird and the city are now even more connected…

“This is the legacy we will leave in Milan. The stadium, obviously, represents a huge legacy that will transform our financial profile, but then there’s also the San Donato development project and the rest.

“If we want AC Milan to become great again, we need to close the revenue gap with the Premier League clubs. When I bought the club four years ago, I used the expression ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ and no one understood what I meant. Now perhaps we are starting to see it.”

“Everyone thought I was making an arrogant, self-centred comparison between me and Berlusconi, but that wasn’t my point. What I was trying to explain was that, just as Berlusconi transformed AC Milan and Serie A, we want to be able, through our ownership, to lead the club into a new era.

“We need to do it in the same way Berlusconi did, albeit in a modern way. I’m used to working a certain way because that’s how I do things, at the highest levels worldwide and in America.”

USA defender Auston Trusty revealed the mindset Mauricio Pochettino has brought to the USMNT and Manchester United fans will like the sound of it.

Pochettino has been confirmed as the new manager of the Red Devils, but is finishing off his stint in charge of USA before travelling to Manchester.

On Saturday the Americans hammered Haiti 6-0 in Miami, before Pochettino’s last game at the helm against the same opponents in Cincinnati on Wednesday.

Celtic defender Trusty opened the scoring on Saturday and was full of praise for his outgoing Manchester.

‘We play for him. Obviously, he’s our gaffer. Obviously, it’s sad that he’s moving on. So it’s a great opportunity that he is moving on into,’ Trusty told TNT Sports after the win over Haiti.

#1928. Hassocks downed by Dockers for second time this season

Three times Hassocks have lost in the Southern Combination Premier Division so far this season. Two of those defeats have come at the hands of Newhaven.

The 2-1 scoreline at the Trafalgar Ground was the same as when the Dockers sailed back from Mid Sussex with all three points in August. The Robins must be delighted to see the back of Newhaven in the league.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

So often the scourge of Hassocks in the past, Lee Robinson scored both the Dockers goals in the space of seven second half minutes.

Lewis Finney pulled one back with 13 minutes remaining and although the Robins threw the kitchen sink at Newhaven, they were unable to find another way through.

The Dockers defence were outstanding and in particular ex-Hassocks centre back Matt Gunn, who deservedly picked up the host's man-of-the-match award afterwards.

Gunn was also a threat at the other end and had two chances to score twice himself inside the opening three minutes. He first saw a flicked header from a corner sensationally tipped around the post by Ed Cooper.

That resulted in another corner and although the Robins cleared this one, Newhaven were able to recycle possession and get a delivery from Ezra Roeg into the box. Gunn remained forward and met it with a powerful headed effort just over the bar.

Hassocks were unable to cope with the relentless tempo at which the Dockers had started. A situation summed up when Harry Reed and Tom Sekyere converged rapidly on Jack Troak to snare the ball from him.

The intense press got Tyler Capon in down the right flank for a cross which Cooper and Harvey Blake combined to clear in somewhat unorthodox, acrobatic style to prevent Robinson from having a tap-in.

Troak managed to lead an attack which finally broke the Robins out of their own half. His cross hung up into the middle was met by Dan Perry for a header just over.

Perry was making his Hassocks debut after signing from East Grinstead Town in midweek. The Hitman has netted 11 times this season for the Wasps and looks to be a quality addition.

Dan Turner then saw a shot from the edge of the box blocked by the nether regions of Elliott Bresciani. The defender putting his body on the line was an early sign of the sort of defending Newhaven would deploy to good effect to get them over the line in the second half.

With the Robins now a willing participant in the game, things began to ebb and flow from end-to-end. Capon was millimetres away from connecting with a Reed centre and Cooper did just enough to put off Sekyere into placing a one-on-one wide.

Perry looked the most likely source of goals for Hassocks. He drew a routine save from Jake Rhodes when heading a Harvey Blake cross on target.

Rhodes then pulled off a much more difficult reaction stop at close range when Big Alex Fair delivered and Perry stooped to direct a header across the Dockers goalkeeper.

Cooper saved well at his near post when Matt Feeney-Hill cut inside before Newhaven faded a little in the final 10 minutes of the half, probably because of the speed at which they played the previous 35.

As a result, Hassocks were on top in the period leading into the break. Finney saw a shot blocked by Gunn and some nifty footwork from Fair followed by a clever back heel teed up Omar Abdsami for a shot just a little too high.

The second half was a slow-burner in comparison to the first until Robinson fired the Dockers ahead on 63 minutes. Sekyere hooked a hopeful ball over the top of the Hassocks defence which the veteran forward showed a remarkable turn of pace to latch onto.

It carried Robinson clear of Turner and enabled him to curl a fine finish with his side foot around Cooper and into the far corner.

Newhaven doubled their lead with 70 on the clock after the Robins were unconvincing dealing with a corner. The delivery from Feeney-Hill was only half cleared to the edge of the box, allowing Ross Barclay to return an up-and-under into the area.

Gunn won a flick on and it found the unmarked Robinson, who had taken advantage of a slapdash Hassocks offside line to move front and centre of goal where he volleyed home unmarked.

Half-hearted appeals for the goal to be disallowed were easily dismissed. Robinson had stayed in a legal position, thanks in part to the Robins being completely out of shape.

Hassocks now had no choice but to lay siege on the Newhaven goal. Liam Benson came on as James Westlake changed formation and went with two up front.

The adjustment helped the Robins. Tall striker Jamie Wilkes put an awkward header wide and Devon Fender rattled the post with a good volley from inside the D.

An excellent move halved the deficit on 77 minutes. Abdsami was patient in waiting for a gap to appear into which he could play a forward pass.

When it came, his ball into the feet of Benson was superbly flicked around the corner by the substitute and into the path of Finney.

The finish from Finney was cool as you like as he picked out the far corner with aplomb to move onto double figures for the season.

Hassocks now had 13 minutes in which to try and find an equaliser. Unfortunately, their shooting from that point on did not match the calmness or precision with which Finney had pulled one back.

Finney came closest to providing a leveller on 88. Abdsami crossed and Perry directed a clever downwards header into the penalty box. The arriving Finney met it with a rasping volley which Rhodes somehow flung himself upwards to block.

Bresciani produced an overhead kick to clear the loose ball off the line and prevent Benson putting away the rebound. In a moment which summed the afternoon up really for Hassocks, that clearance gave another chance to Blake.

The Robins captain could only blaze so high as to pose more of a threat to Newhaven Fort all the way up the hill than the Dockers goal.

Other than the quality of the Finney finish, there was one other positive for the Robins to take home at least. Raging Joe Bull made his 300th senior appearance for the club, becoming the first Robin to pass the triple century landmark since Phil Gault a decade ago.

Hassocks: Cooper; Blake, D Turner, Hendy, Bull; Wilkes, Finney; Fair, Abdsami, Troak; Perry.

Subs: Fender, Benson, Budd (used), Croal, Brodie (unused).

#1927. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

Possession: Chelsea 50%-50% AC MilanShots: 18-5Shots on target: 8-0Corners: 7-2

The final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

What a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj

Ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

A late change for Chelsea as Sarr replaces Fofana.

Chelsea are seeking their fourth goal as Quenda strikes a shot powerfully from just outside the box but it goes narrowly wide. Xabi Alonso’s side have dominated this second half.

Estevao has the chance to score moments after coming on after good work from the Brazilian down Chelsea’s right but is denied by a good save from Torriani.

Chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal once more. Jackson gets the better of Vladimirov down Chelsea’s left and moves into the AC Milan penalty area. Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

Chelsea made a substitution during that break as Anselmino comes on for Hato. Thus far, Chelsea have made three changes in this game and Alonso did confirm before the game that some players should be able to go the full 90 this far into pre-season.

Chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and quickly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

AC Milan have offered very little going forward since the break and Sanchez has not been troubled in the Chelsea goal.

AC Milan have a good chance to get a goal back. Musah finds space on the right side of the box and cuts it back towards the penalty spot. He picks out Nkunku but the former Chelsea man wastes the opportunity.

Palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

Chelsea have their third and their new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

Possession: Chelsea 58%-42% AC MilanShots: 6-4Shots on target: 3-0Corners: 4-2

The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

Due to the water break, there will be three additional minutes at the end of this first half.

The first booking of the game goes the way of AC Milan as Pavlovic clears out Palestra. A deserved booking.

Neto and Pedro exchange a good one-two down Chelsea’s right to put the former racing down the right wing. Neto then tries to find Welbeck in the centre of the box but it is just behind him.

Then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

The space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

Pavlovic drives forward from his defensive position through the Chelsea half. He gets all the way to the Chelsea box before shooting but he looked to lack conviction, firing off target.

We will pause for a drinks break, which unfortunately we became accustomed to during the World Cup. Palmer takes the chance to take a seat on the bench whilst taking on some fluids.

Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

That is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

Neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#1925. Ian Wright praises ‘magnificent’ Ben White after England beat Spain

Ian Wright praised ‘magnificent’ Arsenal defender Ben White after England’s thrilling Nations League win over World Cup holders Spain.

England ended Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday evening.

The Three Lions were bright from the start and took the lead on the stroke of half-time through a penalty from England record goalscorer and Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

Ezri Konsa headed in Declan Rice’s corner shortly after the interval and England were in dreamland when White added a third on the hour mark, arriving at the back-post and firing past Unai Simon.

Spain were being outplayed but had renewed hope when Elliot Anderson was sent off for bringing down Lamine Yamal as he raced through on goal and Mikel Oyarzabal converted the subsequent penalty.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

England fans were having flashbacks of last summer’s World Cup semi-final collapse against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second to set up a tense final 20 minutes.

The hosts pressed for an equaliser but were denied by some valiant England defending and an impressive display from goalkeeper James Trafford.

The hard-fought win means England, already through to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, finish top of their group ahead of World Cup holders Spain.

Wright felt England ‘deserved’ the win despite the late pressure from Spain and singled out Arsenal star White for special praise.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

White was part of England’s World Cup group in Qatar four years ago but left Gareth Southgate’s squad for personal reasons.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Southgate’s reign, a decision that has led to him being booed by some England fans in recent games.

‘Can I just say, I’m really pleased for Ben White and the way things have turned around for him,’ Wright said on ITV.

‘It’s just brilliant for him to get back in and he was magnificent tonight. Not just with the goal but he was making tackles, niggling the Spain players. I’m so pleased it’s ended that way for him.

"This England team are RUNNING RIOT in Spain" 🤩👀 They lead the World Cup winners by 3-0 in Madrid!! WOW. pic.twitter.com/2GuDnscRb4

‘There was a lot to be excited about for England. They were 3-0 up and cruising against the world champions before the red kind of changed the game.’

Meanwhile, Arsenal midfielder Rice said the England squad ‘knew’ they were going to end Spain’s two-year unbeaten run.

‘We knew we were going to beat them tonight,’ he said on ITV. ‘The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive.

‘The first 10 minutes was the best we’ve played. Overall 10 men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against a team unbeaten in 43 is massive.

‘Argentina that day [at the World Cup] wasn’t meant to be. That’s football. When they [Spain] got a second maybe it could have gone another way. It’s a massive win.’

#1924. ‘Predictable, mutual, unfair’ - A brief history of Brighton’s sacked managers

So the current worst kept secret in football is out. Michael Carrick is no more at Old Trafford, it’s actually not United’s first rodeo in this footballing genre.

I recall being at the Amex on Easter Monday 2014, in the period of about 15 minutes I and four others in our party of ten that day received a forwarded text stating that David Moyes would be sacked as Manchester United manager the following morning, Tuesday 22nd April, and he was!

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Sackings are, unfortunately part and parcel of football. In my time following the Albion, we’ve had dismissals that have been predictable, justified, unfair and even a tad bizarre.

My first was Pat Saward in October 1973. I didn’t know much about, but in researching my book a couple of years ago, it was clear that once the ultra ambitious Albion chairman Mike Bamber got a sniff he might be able to rock the football world and bring Brian Clough to the Goldstone, dear old Pat was a dead man walking.

We then didn’t get another sacking for nearly a decade, and then it was all decided on the doorsteps of Sussex.

Mike Bailey had got the club it’s highest ever league finish, 13th in 81/82. But he was building from the back and at times the football wasn’t that exciting. Crowds dipped below the all important break even 15,000, and when fans were questioned by the lottery sellers on their weekly rounds, the word ‘boring’ was predominant and Bailey was out.

All these years later, I still believe the decision was a tad unfair and short sighted, but also one of those classic Brighton and Hove Albion sliding door moments.

Albion legend Steve Foster recently told me, whilst we probably wouldn’t have got to the 1983 Cup Final, we wouldn’t have got relegated and in time, Bailey could have turned us into a consistently top ten side, regularly challenging for Europe.

Bailey’s successor, Jimmy Melia, was almost in a footballing Sword of Damocles situation. Initially a caretaker boss, within a month the Albion embarked on an FA Cup campaign. With Bamber effectively waiting to wield the axe the Monday after the Albion were knocked out, but they weren’t. Melia, with his white dancing shoes took the Albion to Wembley but also rock bottom of the First Division and relegation!

Chris Cattlin was the next cab on the rank, his near three year tender, on a limited budget saw the Albion compete and again, like Bailey, given time, and funding, who knows what he could have achieved?

But he was unceremoniously dismissed at the end of the 85/86 season, but took the Albion to court for unfair dismissal, which resulted in his final victory at the club.

The returning Alan Mullery, another Goldstone legend, in the summer of 1986, was purely cosmetic. Replacing the popular Cattlin with the equally popular Mullery, saw a spike in season ticket sales, and not a lot more.

Mullery was a patsy, disgracefully treated when sacked in January 1987 for almost laughable reasons with the Albion in 13th.

A wretched run under new boss Barry Lloyd followed, with, as with the Division One exit in 1983, the Albion were relegated to the old Third Division in 22nd place in the division.

Yet we had to wait another nine years for another dismissal. Lloyd had left by mutual consent in December 1993, but in December 1996, with the cash strapped and soon to be homeless Albion in 92nd place in the Football League, Jimmy Case was unsurprisingly axed.

As was his successor, Steve Gritt, despite working a footballing miracle and keeping Albion in the league, he was gone in early 1998, again unjust, more about finance than football.

Exiled at Gillingham, crowds nowhere near break even, a massive shot in the arm was required, and that came in the shape of another returning legend (pattern forming) Brian Horton.

Jeff Wood, a genuinely nice guy, was in the wrong place at the wrong time Albion wise in 1999, as was Martin Hinshelwood in 2002.

Full disclosure, I’m in the privileged position to call a number of ex Albion bosses friends, and Mark McGhee is firmly in that catergory. His dismissal in September 2006, is another that sticks in the craw.

I do however still have a degree of sympathy in the bigger picture. At the time, Dick Knight, chasing our collective Falmer dream, was juggling all the balls whilst protecting his own.

Dean Wilkins, still in my opinion technically one of the best coaches the club has ever had, was both a safe pair of hands but a far cheaper option whilst the battle for the stadium went on, tellingly though however he has never worked as a manager since he departed the club in 2008.

I still believe that Mark McGhee would have mounted a promotion challenge to get us back in the Championship.

With the greatest respect in my opinion Albion wise Russel Slade still remains an irrelevance, only doing the job that Micky Adams would have done had he not resigned in February 2009.

Which brings us on to Gus Poyet, a footballing firework, it was great whilst it lasted, but it was what it was, and given off field working relationships, or lack of them, it was never going to last.

But to clarify Gus was not sacked live in the BBC, he was fully aware of the situation and his subsequent reaction was as genuine as American Wrestling!

But he still gave us some great memories, which will never be forgotten.

Chris Hughton’s sacking in 2019, was another exit, which leaves a bad taste. It could have been handled so much better. Like the Moyes text of 2014, I was told that Graham Potter was coming in 40 minutes before Hughton kicked off what was to be his final Albion game. Yet he was interviewed by Richie Reynolds on the pitch at the end about his hopes for the next season!

Potter, could and should have been sacked at least one or two occasions, but a crumb of comfort was the £20 million Chelsea gave us for his services, it truly is a funny old game.

So was Roberto De Zerbi sacked in May 2024, or merely his contract not renewed?

I still love his time as Albion manager, like Gus and others some amazing memories, but unfortunately there are boundaries and as soon as that microphone went under his nose in Rome with the apparent diatribe against Tony Bloom there was only going to be one outcome.

Which brings us around to Fab. Yes many, myself included, have embarked on the ‘Hurzeler Hokey Cokey’, but given the Albion’s current fortunes that’s well and truly parked.

You can never say never following the Albion but I think it’s a fairly safe bet there won’t be another Amex sacking anytime soon!

#1923. Hull City handed injury concern as Senegal boss Patrick Vieira issues Nobel Mendy update

Hull City defender Nobel Mendy is making an early return from international duty due to an injury concern.

The 22-year-old signed for Hull in the summer transfer window, joining from Rayo Vallecano for a club-record fee and penning a five-year deal.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He has since made eight appearances for the Tigers and completed 90 minutes in their 1-0 defeat to Arsenal prior to the international break.

Mendy then linked up with Senegal and was an unused substitute as they thumped Sudan 4-1 last week. However, he was absent for their reunion with Sudan yesterday (November 16).

Speaking ahead of the game, as reported by Ben Dinnery of Premier Injuries, Senegal boss Patrick Vieira confirmed Mendy had picked up an injury.

He said: “He felt a problem with his knee. We have therefore decided, after consultation with our medical department and that of his club, not to take any risks and to let him return to the club.

“We hope it's not very serious and that he can play again as soon as possible.”

Hull have not won in the Premier League since late August and cannot afford to lose too many influential figures. Supporters - as well as manager Sergej Jakirovic - now face an anxious wait to learn the extent of Mendy’s injury.

If Mendy does face a spell on the sidelines, the blow will be somewhat softened by the return of Charlie Hughes. The highly-rated centre-back has not made a single senior appearance this term having undergone a hernia operation, but featured for Hull’s under-21s last week.

Hull are due to return to action on Sunday (November 22), hosting Brighton & Hove Albion at the MKM Stadium.

#1922. Declan Rice says England ‘knew’ they would beat World Cup holders Spain

Declan Rice says the England squad ‘knew’ they would beat World Cup holders Spain in their final Nations League group game.

England earned top spot in their Nations League group and ended Spain’s extraordinary 43-game unbeaten run with a thrilling 3-2 win in Madrid.

Thomas Tuchel’s side scored three goals in 12 minutes either side of half-time to stun Spain before withstanding a late siege to seal their finest win under the German boss.

Harry Kane took his international tally to 93 goals with a penalty on the stroke of half-time as England deservedly ended the opening 45 minutes ahead.

Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White then scored twice in the space of four minutes to open up a commanding 3-0 lead over the shell-shocked Spaniards.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Elliot Anderson’s red card on 63 minutes and Mikel Oyarzabal’s subsequent penalty offered Spain a route back into a match they looked out of.

England fans feared a collapse similar to the one the team suffered in last summer’s World Cup semi-final against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second with 20 minutes remaining.

But this time England kept their opponents at bay with some resolute defending and two superb saves from goalkeeper James Trafford.

Rice was full of praise for his teammates after the Nations League win and said he ‘knew’ England would beat the world champions in their own backyard.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘We knew we were going to beat them tonight,’ Rice told ITV. ‘The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive.

"We knew we were going to beat them tonight!"Declan Rice after England's win over Spain in Madrid 🇪🇸🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 pic.twitter.com/dbNiMi74od

‘Our first ten minutes were probably the best we’ve played. It was pressure, pressure, pressure – we could have had two or three.

‘If we don’t go down to ten men, we see more of the ball, we start to see them jump more, we start to see more space, and we start to see our attacking players thrive like they were doing in the second half.

‘With ten men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against that team is massive. It’s a massive win. Credit to everyone.

‘When they got the second, you might have thought that it was going to go the other way with the amount of pressure they were putting on, but that resilience.

‘Keep emptying the tank, doing anything for this badge, for this team, for our players, for the manager.’

Meanwhile, Tuchel hailed England’s ‘brilliant performance’ after they beat a side who last lost in regulation play in March 2024.

‘Brilliant performance. Well deserved win,’ he said. ‘Overall we were the better team. Fantastic performance from start to finish.

‘It was a long 30 minutes after the red card but I don’t want to focus on that. There were so many positive things in the first 60 minutes.

‘Complete performance. We brought everything to the table. We were brave. Spirit wise, energy wise and also football quality was highest level.

‘We deserved it. We focused on our performance and attitude. I can’t praise the team high enough for what they put out there.’

#1921. Napoli 3-3 AC Milan Women: Lead lost twice as Rossonere claim just one point

AC Milan Women were held to a 3-3 draw in their away game against Napoli on Saturday afternoon, despite having the lead twice.

It has been a rough start to the season for Suzanne Bakker and her side, clinching a mere seven points in the first seven games. Even worse, the form seems to be declining as with today’s game included, they haven’t won in the last three games (1D, 2L).

In the derby against Inter last week, the Rossonere only had themselves to blame for the 0-3 defeat after missing several good chances, while conceding two penalties and getting a red card. They didn’t exactly make things better today either.

After just five minutes of play, the former Milan player Chante Dompig opened the scoring for the hosts. In fairness to the Rossonere, it was a cracking finish from outside the box to stun Sally Rainey in goal, so not much could be done.

Milan responded in the best way possible as Sara Kanutte Fornes pounced on a huge mistake by the Napoli defence, tapping in the equaliser after 16 minutes of play. Just ten minutes later, Abi Brighton found the striker on a corner, heading it home nicely for an early brace.

The Rossonere played well after that and headed into the break with a 2-1 lead. It wasn’t a poor start to the second half, but in the 58th minute, a really poor offside trap (of sorts) meant Napoli only had to play one pass to play Kinga Kozak through, and she made no mistakes.

Sloppy defending that Milan thought they had cancelled out in the 78th minute after a lovely move. Thea Kyvåg found Christy Grimshaw in the box with a great cross and the veteran headed it to Emma Koivisto, who in turn headed it into the back of the net.

The lead only lasted about six minutes, though, as Napoli suddenly had loads of space on the right flank and played a smart low cross into the box. Considering the lack of coverage on the flank, the Milan players at least should have kept tabs on things in the box, but they didn’t.

And so, Michela Giordano made it 3-3 and that was also the final result in the end. Two points dropped for Milan against another struggling side.

#1920. ‘Restricted’ - Mats Wieffer makes Brighton and Chema Andres claim as best position revealed

Brighton star Mats Wieffer admits he felt ‘restricted’ in the full back role as he targets a regular spot in central midfield.

The Dutch international joined Brighton as a midfielder for around £25m in 2024 but often played as a reluctant right full back.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It's a position Wieffer adapted to pretty well but now the former Feyenoord man is keen to make an impact in his preferred central midfield role.

Ferdi Kadioglu and Costinha are now the recognised right backs at Brighton, which means Wieffer can now compete for midfield minutes, alongside the likes of Pascal Gross, Yasin Ayari, Jack Hinshelwood, Diego Gomez and Chema Andres, who has impressed since his summer arrival.

Chema joined for around £20m from VfB Stuttgart and Wieffer feels they operate in a similar position.

Wieffer - who is fit once again following a recent knee injury - said to the club website: "I can still play both, but I'm happy to play in midfield.

"Now I need to keep the rhythm, train hard, and get all the principles there, because for the last two seasons I was more focused on full-back.

“I think Chema [Andres] and I are a little bit similar, but the rest are a little bit different. If I have to compare myself, I'm more like Chema than the others.”

He added: “You're always happy to play, but overall I prefer midfield because I've always done it. As a full-back, you're a little bit restricted, and I think I'm a better player as a midfielder overall.

“But last season went really well, and he always told me I was playing well and the system suited me. The stats were good, which gave me confidence that he put me in the starting XI.

“The team and playing are always the most important things for me. In the end I'm happy, but if I could choose I would play in midfield.”

Brighton are second in the table and resume Premier league action after the international break at Hull City.

It's been an impressive start to the season as Brighton have 22 points from 10 matches and are the division's leading scorers.

Wieffer said: “Last season we had the same kind of principles we have now, but this season we are doing it every game.

“When everybody sees that the things we train are working it gives the feeling that if we keep doing this it will pay off in points.

“Most importantly, it's because of the things we do like the pressing. Last season we didn't do it every game.

“In the bigger games we were always there but sometimes in the games we thought we needed to win it was a little bit less and opponents punished us.

“That was frustrating - getting points from a bigger team and then dropping points against a team we thought we were equals with.”

#1919. ‘I don’t see there’s any need’ - Ex-Leeds United and England goalkeeper preaches James Trafford patience

Former Leeds United goalkeeper Paul Robinson does not believe there is “any need” for Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel to immediately replace Jordan Pickford with James Trafford.

Game time has been evenly split between Everton’s Pickford and Leeds’ Trafford across the last two international breaks, with the latter pushing to dislodge the former.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Trafford has made a stellar start to life at Leeds since his summer switch from Manchester City and shone in England’s 3-2 Nations League win over Spain at the weekend.

The 24-year-old has been showered with praise but Robinson, who also represented England in his playing days, has preached patience.

Writing for The i, he said: “At the moment, I don’t see there’s any need to replace Jordan. Without a doubt, the next major tournament he will be playing, but he’ll be 34.

“It just goes to show Tuchel sees this as a long-term project. He’s not in overnight thinking, how do I win the next game? He’s preparing for life further down the road – and life after Jordan Pickford.”

Robinson may not be advocating for an immediate change between the sticks, yet is a strong admirer of Leeds’ club-record signing.

He has suggested Trafford - who cost the Whites a hefty £40m - has the potential to enter the elite goalkeeper bracket.

The 47-year-old said: “As English goalkeepers, we haven’t had one quite in the bracket of Ederson, Alisson, Thibaut Courtois at their peaks. The bracket underneath, we’re flush with.

“Trafford has the potential to enter that top bracket, while Pickford has improved as a person and a player. There was a lot of talk about his antics on the pitch – he’s understood who he is, and he’s channelled the best part of him in the right way.”

#1918. Luis de la Fuente singles out ‘fantastic’ England star after Spain defeat

Luis de la Fuente reserved special praise for James Trafford following Spain’s 3-2 defeat to England, hailing the goalkeeper’s ‘fantastic’ display in Madrid.

England produced arguably their finest all-round performance under Thomas Tuchel in Sunday’s Nations League classic to land a hefty psychological blow on the reigning world and European champions.

The Three Lions flew out of the blocks from minute one and were duly rewarded for their efforts as captain Harry Kane converted from the spot to break the deadlock on the stroke of half-time.

Goals from Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased the deficit after the restart, with Spain all at sea before Elliot Anderson’s sending off handed the hosts a lifeline.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored with the resulting penalty before Nico Williams finished off a flowing Spanish move to set up a tense final 15 minutes at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But ten-man England managed to keep La Roja at bay thanks largely to an inspired Trafford, who was selected over Jordan Pickford and repaid Tuchel’s faith with a series of stunning late stops to help preserve the visitors’ narrow advantage

Trafford’s double save to keep out Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte earned the Leeds United keeper immediate high fives and adulation from his team-mates.

The result brought Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten streak to a halt and ensured England finished top of their Nations League group having picked up 15 from a possible 18 points.

‘Positives? There are a lot of positives to find here. It’s very difficult to get here, to achieve the numbers that we’ve achieved,’ Spain boss De La Fuente said when asked about Spain’s run being brought to an end.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It’s something historical that we’ve done. We’ve been champions of the Nations League, the Euros, the World Cup, everything is positive.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘But we know how to win and we know how to lose. And we have to say that we faced a rival that we managed to beat in the past but I have to say that they were the better team in the first 30 minutes.

‘I had a feeling we could get there when they went one man down but I’m really proud of this team, their hunger, their eagerness.

‘I’m convinced that the best is yet to come for this team.’

De la Fuente made four second-half substitutions as they looked to claw their way back into the contest, with Fermin Lopez, Nico Williams, Pedri and Dean Huijsen all sent on in the Spanish capital.

But the home team were thwarted by Trafford’s heroics in the closing stages – and De la Fuente took the opportunity to applaud the ‘keeper’s outstanding showing.

‘What we wanted to do with the substitutions was try to go all out, try to generate more chances,’ he explained.

‘We did generate some chances but England’s goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last ten or 15 minutes.

‘In any case, there were many alternatives but again, I want to say how fantastic England were on the night.’

Asked what he and Tuchel had discussed shortly after the final whistle, De La Fuente replied: ‘We just spoke for a few seconds about what happened this week and we just wanted to clarify things.

‘I have no problem with him at all, all I have is admiration and respect.

‘As for the dressing room, when you are not used to losing, you look at eachother and ask, “What happened here?”, so what did I tell my players? I told them that we haven’t lost for three years and we’ve won all the important tournaments.

‘All I wanted to do was say how proud I am of them because of this and it’s a shame we don’t have another game coming up, we have to wait until March.’

The Spain head coach added: ‘We’ll surely come back in March with renewed energy, thinking about the Nations League final.

‘We’re going to try to get there, knowing difficult it is to get there and win a competition like this.

‘But the spirit, the intention, the ambition are all there.’
